options.A: He seldom writes a book straight through.
options.B: He writes several books simultaneously.
options.C: He draws on his real-life experiences.
options.D: He often turns to his wife for help.

questions.cn: 男士写作时会怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 他很少一口气写完一本书。
optionsCn.C: 他借鉴自己的真实经历。

options.A: Writing a book is just like watching a football match.
options.B: Writers actually work every bit as hard as footballers.

options.D: Unlike a football match, there is no end to writing a book.

optionsCn.B: 作家其实和足球运动员一样努力。

optionsCn.D: 与足球比赛不同，写书没有终场。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: F: Mr. Ishiguro, have you ever found one of your books at a second-hand bookstore?
lines.cn: F：石黑先生，你有没有在二手书店里看到过自己的书？

lines.t: M: Yes, that kind of thing is difficult. If they've got my book there, I think, well, this is an insult. Somebody didn't want to keep my book. But if it's not there, I feel it's an insult too. I think, why aren't people exchanging my book? Why isn't it in this store?
lines.cn: M：有，这种事很让人为难。如果店里有我的书，我就会想：嗯，这是一种侮辱，有人不想留着我的书。可如果店里没有，我也觉得是一种侮辱。我会想：为什么人们不拿来交换我的书？为什么这家店里没有？

lines.t: F: Does being a writer require a thick skin?
lines.cn: F：当作家需要脸皮厚吗？

lines.t: M: Yes. For example, my wife can be very harsh. I began working on my latest book, The Buried Giant, in 2004. But I stopped after I showed my wife a little section. She thought it was rubbish.
lines.cn: M：是的。比如，我妻子有时很刻薄。我 2004 年开始写最新的那本书《被掩埋的巨人》，可我把一小段拿给妻子看之后就停笔了。她觉得那都是垃圾。

lines.t: F: Even after you won a Booker Prize?
lines.cn: F：即便在你拿了布克奖之后也是这样？

lines.t: M: She's not intimidated at all. And she criticizes me in exactly the same way she did when I was first unpublished and I was starting out.
lines.cn: M：她一点也不怕我。她批评我的方式，和当年我还没出过书、刚起步时完全一样。

lines.t: F: But you would never compromise on your vision.
lines.cn: F：但你绝不会在自己的构想上妥协。

lines.t: M: No, I wouldn't ever compromise on the essential — the ideas or the themes. This isn't really what my wife is trying to criticize me about. It's always about execution.
lines.cn: M：不会，我绝不会在本质的东西——想法或主题——上妥协。而这其实并不是妻子想批评我的地方。她说的总是具体的落实。

lines.t: F: So why did you put your book, The Buried Giant, aside for so long? Apparently you started working on it over ten years ago.
lines.cn: F：那你为什么把《被掩埋的巨人》搁置了这么久？据说你十多年前就开始写了。

lines.t: M: I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years. And by the time I come back to it, it may have changed. Usually my imagination has moved on and I can think of different contexts or a different way to do it.
lines.cn: M：我经常把一本书写到一半就停笔，搁上几年。等我再回到它那里时，它可能已经变了。通常是我的想象已经往前走，我能想出不同的背景或不同的写法。

lines.t: F: What does it feel like when you finally finish a book?
lines.cn: F：终于写完一本书时是什么感觉？

lines.t: M: It's funny you ask that, because I never have this moment when I feel, ah, I've finished. I watch footballers at the end of the match, you know, the whistle goes and they've won or lost. Until then, they've been giving everything they have, and at that moment they know it's over. It's funny for an author — there's never a finishing whistle.
lines.cn: M：你问得挺有意思，因为我从来没有那种“啊，我写完了”的时刻。我看足球运动员在比赛结束时的样子：哨声一响，他们或赢或输。在那之前，他们一直拼尽全力，而在那一刻他们知道一切都结束了。对作家来说就很奇怪——永远没有一声终场哨。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are the speakers talking about?

options.A: Achievements of black male athletes in college.
options.B: Financial assistance to black athletes in college.
options.C: High college dropout rates among black athletes.

questions.cn: 两位说话人在谈什么？

optionsCn.A: 大学里黑人男性运动员的成就。
optionsCn.B: 对大学黑人运动员的经济资助。
optionsCn.C: 黑人运动员中很高的大学辍学率。
optionsCn.D: 黑人运动员的本科入学人数。

questions.stem: What is the new finding about black male athletes in this study?

options.A: They display great talent in every kind of game.
options.B: They are better at sports than at academic work.
options.C: They have difficulty finding money to complete their studies.
options.D: They make money for the college but often fail to earn a degree.

questions.cn: 这项研究关于黑人男性运动员的新发现是什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们在各类比赛中都展现出极强的天赋。
optionsCn.B: 他们擅长运动胜过学业。
optionsCn.C: 他们难以筹到完成学业所需的钱。
optionsCn.D: 他们为学校赚钱，却常常拿不到学位。

questions.stem: What is the graduation rate of black male athletes?

options.A: About 15%.
options.B: Around 40%.

questions.cn: 黑人男性运动员的毕业率是多少？

questions.stem: What accounts for black athletes' failure to obtain a college degree according to the man?

options.A: Coaches lack the incentive to graduate them.
options.B: College degrees do not count much to them.
options.C: They have little interest in academic work.
options.D: Schools do not deem it a serious problem.

questions.cn: 根据男士的说法，黑人运动员拿不到大学学位的原因是什么？

optionsCn.A: 教练缺乏让他们毕业的动力。
optionsCn.B: 大学学位对他们来说不太重要。
optionsCn.C: 他们对学业没什么兴趣。
optionsCn.D: 学校不认为这是个严重问题。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: According to a study of race and equity in education, black athletes are dropping out of college across the country at alarming rates. With us to talk about the findings in this study is Washington Post columnist Kevin Blackstone. Good morning.
lines.cn: F：一项关于教育中的种族与公平的研究显示，全美各地的黑人运动员正以惊人的比例从大学辍学。今天和我们一起讨论这项研究结果的是《华盛顿邮报》专栏作家凯文·布莱克斯通。早上好。

lines.t: M: Good morning. How are you?
lines.cn: M：早上好。你好吗？

lines.t: F: Fine, thank you. What is new that you found in this study?
lines.cn: F：很好，谢谢。你在这项研究中发现了什么新东西？

lines.t: M: Well, this is Shaun Harper's study, and he points out that on major college campuses across the country, black males make up less than 3% of undergraduate enrollments. Yet, when you look at their numbers or percentages on the revenue-generating sports teams of football and basketball, they make up well into 50 to 60% of those teams. So the idea is that they are really there to be part of the revenue-generating working class of athletes on campus, and not necessarily there to be part of the educating class, as most students in other groups are.
lines.cn: M：嗯，这是肖恩·哈珀的研究。他指出，在全国各地的重点大学校园里，黑人男性在本科生入学人数中占比不到 3%。然而，若看他们在橄榄球和篮球这两项能创收的运动队中的人数或比例，他们在这些队伍里占到 50% 到 60%。所以问题在于，他们来这里的真正身份其实是校园里为学校创收的运动员“打工阶层”，而不一定像其他群体的大多数学生那样，是受教育群体的一员。

lines.t: F: Compared with other groups, I think the numbers in this group at those 65 schools are something like just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all.
lines.cn: F：与其他群体相比，我想在那 65 所学校里，这个群体的数字大致是：黑人男性运动员中仅仅略多于一半能够毕业。

lines.t: M: Exactly. And what's really bad about this is these athletes are supposedly promised at least one thing as reward for all their blood and sweat, and that is a college degree, which can be a transformative tool in our society when you talk about upward mobility. And that's really the troubling part about this.
lines.cn: M：正是。更糟的是，这些运动员付出了血汗，本应至少得到一样回报，那就是大学文凭——在我们的社会里，说到向上流动，这可能是一种能改变命运的工具。而这正是真正令人不安的地方。

lines.t: F: Well, this has been talked about so much, really, in recent years. Why hasn't it changed?
lines.cn: F：嗯，近年来这件事确实已经被谈论得很多了。为什么情况没有改变？

lines.t: M: Well, I think one of the reasons it hasn't changed is because there's really no economic pressure to change this. All of the incentive is really on winning and not losing on the field or on the court. Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players.
lines.cn: M：嗯，我认为它没有改变的原因之一是，确实不存在改变它的经济压力。所有的激励都在于在赛场或球场上赢球、不输球。教练并不一定有让球员毕业的动力。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the speaker mainly talking about?

options.A: Marketing strategies.
options.B: Holiday shopping.

questions.cn: 讲话者主要在谈什么？

questions.stem: How many people will shop on Cyber Monday?

options.A: About 50% of holiday shoppers.
options.B: About 20-30% of holiday shoppers.

questions.cn: 有多少人会在“网络星期一”购物？

optionsCn.B: 约 20% 至 30% 的假日购物者。

questions.stem: What does Fortune say about traditional shopping malls?

options.A: They have fewer customers.
options.B: They find it hard to survive.

questions.cn: 《财富》杂志对传统购物中心说了什么？

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: America's holiday shopping season starts on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving.
lines.cn: 美国的假日购物季从“黑色星期五”开始，也就是感恩节的第二天。

lines.t: It is the busiest shopping day of the year.
lines.cn: 这是一年中最繁忙的购物日。

lines.t: Retailers make the most money this time of year, about 20 to 30 percent of annual revenue.
lines.cn: 零售商每年这个时候赚得最多，约占全年收入的 20% 到 30%。

lines.t: About 136 million people will shop during the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
lines.cn: 约有 1.36 亿人会在感恩节长周末购物。

lines.t: More and more will shop online.
lines.cn: 越来越多人会在网上购物。

lines.t: In an era of instant information, shoppers can use their mobile phones to find deals.
lines.cn: 在这个信息即时的时代，购物者可以用手机寻找优惠。

lines.t: About 183.8 million people will shop on Cyber Monday, the first Monday after Thanksgiving.
lines.cn: 约有 1.838 亿人会在“网络星期一”——感恩节后的第一个周一——购物。

lines.t: More than half of all holiday purchases will be made online.
lines.cn: 超过一半的假日购物将在网上完成。

lines.t: One in five Americans will use a tablet or smartphone.
lines.cn: 五分之一的美国人会使用平板电脑或智能手机。

lines.t: Online spending on Black Friday will rise 15 percent to hit 2.7 billion dollars this year.
lines.cn: 今年“黑色星期五”的线上消费将增长 15%，达到 27 亿美元。

lines.t: Cyber Monday spending will increase 12 percent to 3 billion dollars.
lines.cn: “网络星期一”的消费将增长 12%，达到 30 亿美元。

lines.t: For many, shopping online was a more comfortable alternative than crowded malls.
lines.cn: 对许多人来说，网上购物比拥挤的商场更舒适。

lines.t: The shift to online shopping has had a big impact on traditional shopping malls.
lines.cn: 向网上购物的转变对传统购物中心造成了很大冲击。

lines.t: Since 2010, more than 24 shopping malls have closed and an additional 60 are struggling.
lines.cn: 自 2010 年以来，已有 24 家以上购物中心关闭，另有 60 家在苦苦支撑。

lines.t: However, Fortune says the weakest of the malls have closed; the sector is thriving again.
lines.cn: 不过《财富》杂志称，倒闭的是最弱的那些购物中心；这个行业正在重新繁荣起来。

lines.t: The International Council of Shopping Centers said 94.2 percent of malls were full or occupied with shops by the end of 2014.
lines.cn: 国际购物中心协会表示，到 2014 年底，94.2% 的购物中心已满租或有商户入驻。

lines.t: That is the highest level in 27 years.
lines.cn: 这是 27 年来的最高水平。

lines.t: Economist Gus Faucher said lower unemployment and rising wages could give Americans more money to spend.
lines.cn: 经济学家格斯·福彻说，失业率下降和工资上涨可能让美国人有更多钱可花。

lines.t: The average American consumer will spend about 805 dollars on gifts.
lines.cn: 美国消费者平均会在礼物上花费约 805 美元。

lines.t: That's about 630.5 billion dollars between November and December, an increase of 3.7 percent from last year.
lines.cn: 11 月至 12 月间的总额约为 6305 亿美元，比去年增长 3.7%。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is said to account for the increased number of shoppers?

options.A: Better quality of consumer goods.
options.B: Higher employment and wages.

questions.cn: 据说购物人数增加的原因是什么？

questions.stem: What do we learn about the superbugs?

options.A: They are new species of big insects.
options.B: They are overprescribed antibiotics.

questions.cn: 关于超级细菌，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们是大型昆虫的新物种。
optionsCn.B: 它们是被过度处方的抗生素。
optionsCn.C: 它们是危及生命的疾病。

questions.stem: What is the result of the overuse of antibiotics?

options.A: Antibiotics are now in short supply.
options.B: Many infections are no longer curable.
options.C: Large amounts of tax money are wasted.

questions.cn: 滥用抗生素的结果是什么？

questions.stem: What is most urgently needed for tackling the large life-threatening epidemic according to the speaker?

options.A: Facilities.
options.B: Expertise.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，应对这场大规模危及生命的疫情最迫切需要的是什么？

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: For years, many of us have relied on antibiotic use to treat various infections.
lines.cn: 多年来，我们许多人一直依靠抗生素来治疗各种感染。

lines.t: And the reality is that antibiotics have been responsible for saving millions of lives since penicillin, one of the earliest antibiotics, was first used on a clinical basis 70 years ago.
lines.cn: 而事实是，自 70 年前最早的抗生素之一青霉素首次用于临床以来，抗生素已拯救了数百万人的生命。

lines.t: However, today is a new era in which taking antibiotics can cause some very dangerous and potentially life-threatening situations.
lines.cn: 然而，今天已进入一个新时代：服用抗生素可能引发一些非常危险、甚至危及生命的情况。

lines.t: In fact, you may have heard about the new superbugs, which are antibiotic-resistant bacteria that have developed as a result of overprescribed antibiotics.
lines.cn: 事实上，你可能听说过新的“超级细菌”，它们是因抗生素被过度处方而产生的耐药细菌。

lines.t: In the past, health experts warned us that the day would come in which it would become very difficult to provide medical care for even common problems, such as lung infection or severe sore throat.
lines.cn: 过去，卫生专家曾警告我们，总有一天连肺部感染或严重咽喉疼痛这类常见问题都会变得极难治疗。

lines.t: And apparently that day has come, because seemingly routine operations such as knee replacements are now much more hazardous due to the looming threat of these infections.
lines.cn: 显然，那一天已经到来：由于这些感染的威胁日益逼近，像膝关节置换这样看似常规的手术如今危险得多。

lines.t: The problem has grown into such epidemic proportions that this severe strain of resistant bacteria is being blamed for nearly 700,000 deaths each year throughout the world.
lines.cn: 问题已发展到如此严重的程度：这种强耐药菌株被归咎于全世界每年近 70 万人的死亡。

lines.t: And unfortunately, health experts worry that the number will rise to 10 million or more on a yearly basis by 2050.
lines.cn: 不幸的是，卫生专家担心到 2050 年，这一数字每年将升至 1000 万甚至更多。

lines.t: With such a large life-threatening epidemic, it is sad to say that only 1.2% of budgetary money for the National Institutes of Health is currently being spent on research to tackle this problem.
lines.cn: 面对如此大规模、危及生命的疫情，遗憾的是，美国国立卫生研究院目前只有 1.2% 的预算资金用于攻克这一问题的研究。

lines.t: This is a far cry from the funds necessary for a problem of such magnitude.
lines.cn: 这与应对如此规模的问题所需的资金相差甚远。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a university?

options.A: It is accessible only to the talented.
options.B: It improves students’ ability to think.
options.C: It starts a lifelong learning process.
options.D: It gives birth to many eminent scholars.

questions.cn: 关于大学，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它只对有才华的人开放。
optionsCn.B: 它提升学生的思考能力。
optionsCn.C: 它开启终身学习的过程。
optionsCn.D: 它孕育出许多杰出学者。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the speaker's stories about universities?

options.A: They encourage academic democracy.
options.B: They promote globalization.

questions.cn: 从讲话者的故事中，我们了解到大学的什么？

questions.stem: What does the speaker see in the young man who challenged his paper?

options.A: His thirst for knowledge.
options.B: His eagerness to find a job.

questions.cn: 在挑战他论文的那个年轻人身上，讲话者看到了什么？

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: This is the reason you are here in a university. You are here to be educated. You are here to understand thinking better and to think better yourself.
lines.cn: 这就是你身处大学的原因。你来这里是为了接受教育，是为了更好地理解思考，并让自己思考得更好。

lines.t: It's not a chance you're going to have throughout your lifetime. For the next few years, you have a chance to focus on thinking.
lines.cn: 这不是你一生中随时都会有的机会。在接下来的几年里，你有机会专注于思考。

lines.t: I think about some of the students who took advantage of their opportunities in a university. One of the stories I always like to tell is of a freshman seminar that I had a chance to teach at Harvard when I was president of the university.
lines.cn: 我常想起一些在大学里善用机会的学生。我最喜欢讲的一个故事，是我担任哈佛大学校长时有机会教的一门新生研讨课。

lines.t: I taught a seminar on globalization and I assigned a reading that I had written about global capital flows. And as I did each week, I asked one of the students to introduce the readings.
lines.cn: 我教的是全球化研讨课，布置了一篇我自己写的关于全球资本流动的阅读材料。像每周一样，我请一位学生来做导读。

lines.t: And this young man in October of his freshman year said something like the following. The reading by President Summers on the flow of capital across countries, it was kind of interesting, but the data did not come close to supporting the conclusions.
lines.cn: 这个大一新生在当年 10 月说了大致这样的话：萨默斯校长关于资本跨国流动的那篇文章有点意思，但数据远远不足以支撑其结论。

lines.t: And I thought to myself, what a fantastic thing this was. How could somebody who had been there for five weeks tell the person who had the title president that he didn't really know what he was talking about? And it was a special moment.
lines.cn: 我心里想，这真是件了不起的事。一个才来了五周的人，怎么能对拥有校长头衔的人说，他其实不太清楚自己在讲什么？那是个特别的时刻。

lines.t: Now, I don't want to be misunderstood. I explained to my student that I actually thought he was rather more confused than I was. And I argued back.
lines.cn: 不过我不想被误解。我向那位学生说明，其实我认为他比我更糊涂，并且和他争论了回去。

lines.t: But what was really important about that was the universities stand out as places that really are about the authority of ideas. You see it in faculty members who are pleased when their students make a discovery that undermines a cherished theory that they had put forward.
lines.cn: 但真正重要的是，大学之所以与众不同，就在于它是真正以“思想的权威”为本的地方。你能在那些教授身上看到这一点：当学生有了发现，推翻了他们自己提出的钟爱理论时，他们反而感到高兴。

lines.t: I think of another student I had who came to me one evening, walked into my office and said that I had written a pretty good paper, but that it had five important mistakes and that he wanted a job.
lines.cn: 我还想起另一位学生。有天晚上他走进我的办公室，说我写了一篇相当不错的论文，但有五个重要错误，然后又说他想找份工作。

lines.t: You could debate whether they actually were mistakes, but you couldn't debate that young man's hunger to learn. You could not debate that that young man was someone who wanted to make a difference in economics.
lines.cn: 你可以争论那究竟算不算错误，但你无法否认那个年轻人求知的渴望。你也无法否认，那是个想在经济学领域做出改变的人。

lines.t: And he is today a professor of economics, and his works are more cited as an economist than any other economist in the world.
lines.cn: 如今他是一位经济学教授，作为经济学家，他的著作被引用次数超过世界上任何其他经济学家。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the simple test suggest?

options.A: Few people know how to retrieve information properly.
options.B: People can enhance their memory with a few tricks.
options.C: Most people have a rather poor long-term memory.
options.D: People tend to underestimate their mental powers.

questions.cn: 这个简单的测试说明了什么？

optionsCn.A: 很少有人知道如何正确地提取信息。
optionsCn.B: 人们可以用一些技巧增强记忆力。
optionsCn.C: 大多数人的长期记忆力相当差。
optionsCn.D: 人们往往低估自己的心智能力。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the two lists in the test?

options.A: They present the states in a surprisingly different order.
options.B: They include more or less the same number of states.
options.C: They are exactly the same as is shown in the atlas.
options.D: They contain names of the most familiar states.

questions.cn: 关于测试中的两份清单，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们以惊人不同的顺序列出各州。
optionsCn.B: 它们包含的州数量大体相同。
optionsCn.C: 它们与地图上显示的完全一致。
optionsCn.D: 它们包含最熟悉的那些州的名称。

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about preparing for and taking an exam?

options.A: Focusing on what is likely to be tested.
options.B: Having a good sleep the night before.
options.C: Reviewing your lessons where the exam is to take place.
options.D: Making sensible decisions while choosing your answers.

questions.cn: 关于备考和应考，讲话者给出了什么建议？

optionsCn.A: 专注于可能考到的内容。
optionsCn.C: 在将要考试的场所复习功课。
optionsCn.D: 在选答案时做出明智的判断。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Psychological research shows we consistently underestimate our mental powers.
lines.cn: 心理学研究表明，我们总是低估自己的心智能力。

lines.t: If you think this does not apply to you, then here is a simple test to show you are wrong.
lines.cn: 如果你认为这不适用于你，那么有个简单的测试可以证明你错了。

lines.t: Write down the names of all the American states you can remember.
lines.cn: 写出你能记住的所有美国州的名称。

lines.t: Put the list away and then set yourself the same task a week later.
lines.cn: 把清单收起来，一周后再给自己同样的任务。

lines.t: Provided you have not cheated by consulting an atlas, you will notice something rather surprising.
lines.cn: 只要你没有查地图作弊，你就会注意到一件相当令人惊讶的事。

lines.t: The two lists will contain roughly the same number of states, but they will not be identical.
lines.cn: 两份清单包含的州数量大致相同，但内容并不一致。

lines.t: Some names will have slipped away, but others will have replaced them.
lines.cn: 有些名称被忘掉了，但另一些会补上它们的位置。

lines.t: This suggests that somewhere in your mind you may well have a record of virtually every state.
lines.cn: 这说明在你脑海的某处，很可能记录着几乎每一个州。

lines.t: So it is not really your memory letting you down, just your ability to retrieve information from it.
lines.cn: 所以真正让你失望的不是你的记忆力，而是你从记忆中提取信息的能力。

lines.t: We would remember a lot more if we had more confidence in our memories and knew how to use them properly.
lines.cn: 如果我们对自己的记忆力更有信心、并且懂得如何正确运用它，我们就能记住多得多的东西。

lines.t: One useful tip is that things are more likely to be remembered if you are in exactly the same state and place as you were when you learned them.
lines.cn: 一个有用的提示是：如果你处于与学习时完全相同的状态和地点，就更容易回忆起所记的内容。

lines.t: So if you are a student who always reviews over black coffee, perhaps it would be sensible to prime yourself with a cup before the exam.
lines.cn: 所以，如果你是一个总爱边喝黑咖啡边复习的学生，那在考试前先喝一杯或许是个明智的做法。

lines.t: If possible, you should also try to learn information in the room where it is going to be tested.
lines.cn: 如果可能的话，你还应该尽量在将要接受考试的那个房间里学习这些内容。

lines.t: When you learn is also important.
lines.cn: 什么时候学也很重要。

lines.t: Lots of people swear they can absorb new information more efficiently at some times of the day than at others.
lines.cn: 许多人坚信自己在一天中的某些时段吸收新信息比在其他时段更高效。

lines.t: Research shows this is not just imagination.
lines.cn: 研究表明这并不只是想象。

lines.t: There is a biological rhythm for learning.
lines.cn: 学习存在一种生物节律。

lines.t: Though it affects different people in different ways, for most of us the best plan is to take in new information in the morning and then try to consolidate it into memory during the afternoon.
lines.cn: 尽管它对不同人的影响方式不同，但对我们大多数人来说，最好的安排是在上午吸收新信息，然后在下午把它巩固进记忆。

lines.t: But this does not apply to everyone, so it is essential to establish your own rhythm.
lines.cn: 但这并不适用于所有人，所以确立自己的节律很重要。

lines.t: You can do this by learning a set number of lines of poetry at different times of the day and seeing when most lines stick.
lines.cn: 要做到这一点，你可以在一天中的不同时段背诵固定数量的诗句，看看哪个时段记住的诗句最多。

lines.t: When you have done this, try to organize your life so that the time set aside for learning coincides with the time when your memory is at its best.
lines.cn: 做完这一步之后，试着安排你的生活，让专门用于学习的时间与你记忆力最佳的时段相吻合。

lines.t: Avoid learning marathons. They do not make the best use of your mind.
lines.cn: 避免长时间连续学习的“马拉松”。那并不能最有效地利用你的头脑。

lines.t: Take plenty of breaks because they offer a double bonus.
lines.cn: 多休息，因为休息带来双重的益处。

lines.t: The time off gives your mind a chance to do some preliminary consolidation and it also gives a memory boost to the learning.
lines.cn: 休息时间让你的大脑有机会进行初步巩固，也会给学习带来记忆上的加成。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Hello. Today I am going to talk about poverty.
lines.cn: 大家好。今天我要讲的是贫困。

lines.t: Poverty has become a critical issue in today's world. It concerns not only us sociologists but also economists, politicians and business people.
lines.cn: 贫困已成为当今世界的一个关键问题。它不仅关系到我们社会学家，也关系到经济学家、政治家和商界人士。

lines.t: Poverty has been understood in many different ways. One useful way is to distinguish between three degrees of poverty: extreme poverty, moderate poverty and relative poverty.
lines.cn: 人们对贫困有多种不同的理解方式。一种有用的方法是区分三个层次的贫困：极端贫困、中度贫困和相对贫困。

lines.t: The first type of poverty is extreme poverty. It is also called absolute poverty.
lines.cn: 第一种贫困是极端贫困，也被称为绝对贫困。

lines.t: In extreme poverty, households cannot meet basic needs for survival. People are chronically hungry. They are unable to access safe drinking water, let alone health care. They cannot afford education for their children.
lines.cn: 在极端贫困中，家庭无法满足基本的生存需求。人们长期处于饥饿状态，无法获得安全的饮用水，更谈不上医疗保健，也负担不起孩子的教育。

lines.t: In short, people who live in extreme poverty do not have even the minimum resources to support themselves and their families.
lines.cn: 简而言之，生活在极端贫困中的人连维持自己和家人生活的最低资源都不具备。

lines.t: Where does extreme poverty occur? Well, you can find it only in developing countries.
lines.cn: 极端贫困出现在哪里？嗯，你只能在发展中国家看到它。

lines.t: Well, what about moderate poverty? Unlike extreme poverty, moderate poverty generally refers to conditions of life in which basic needs are met but barely.
lines.cn: 那么中度贫困呢？与极端贫困不同，中度贫困通常指基本需求勉强得到满足的生活状况。

lines.t: People living in moderate poverty have the resources to keep themselves alive, but only at a very basic level.
lines.cn: 生活在中度贫困中的人拥有维持生存的资源，但只处于非常基本的水平。

lines.t: For example, they may have access to drinking water but not clean, safe drinking water. They may have a home to shelter themselves, but it does not have power supply, a telephone or plumbing.
lines.cn: 例如，他们也许能获得饮用水，但不是清洁安全的饮用水。他们也许有房子居住，但房子里没有供电、电话或自来水管道。

lines.t: The third kind of poverty is relative poverty. Relative poverty is generally considered to be a household income level which is below a given proportion of average family income.
lines.cn: 第三种贫困是相对贫困。相对贫困通常被认为是指家庭收入水平低于平均家庭收入的某一比例。

lines.t: The relatively poor live in high-income countries, but they do not have a high income themselves.
lines.cn: 相对贫困者生活在高收入国家，但他们自己并没有高收入。

lines.t: The method of calculating the poverty line is different from country to country, but we can say that basically a family living in relative poverty has less than a certain percentage of the average family income.
lines.cn: 各国计算贫困线的方法不同，但可以说，生活在相对贫困中的家庭，其收入低于平均家庭收入的某一百分比。

lines.t: For example, in the United States, a family can be considered poor if their income is less than 50% of the national average family income.
lines.cn: 例如在美国，如果家庭收入低于全国平均家庭收入的 50%，就可被视为贫困。

lines.t: They can meet their basic needs, but they lack access to cultural goods, entertainment and recreation. They also do not have access to quality health care or other prerequisites for upward social mobility.
lines.cn: 他们能满足基本需求，但无法获得文化产品、娱乐和休闲。他们也得不到优质医疗，以及向上社会流动所需的其他前提条件。

lines.t: Well, I have briefly explained to you how poverty can be distinguished as extreme poverty, moderate poverty and relative poverty.
lines.cn: 好了，我简要说明了贫困如何被区分为极端贫困、中度贫困和相对贫困。

lines.t: We should keep these distinctions in mind when we research people's living conditions, either in the developing or the developed world.
lines.cn: 无论是在发展中国家还是在发达国家，研究人们的生活状况时，我们都应该记住这些区分。
